prompt:
Paint ONE place into this tile of a painted grand-strategy map. The input is the finished map around the place, seen straight down; the place stands at the exact CENTRE of the image.

The place: Lãng Đào Môn, minor seat. Paint it as a minor sect's seat: a compact walled compound of halls and one tall pagoda or tower, terraces where the land climbs.
How it looks: On low wooded ground just back from the river stands a sect gate made of two great river-boat hulls, upturned and set on end so their keels meet overhead in a pointed arch. Behind it, tarred timber halls and rope sheds climb a gentle rise, and a path of crushed shell runs down toward the landing at Đào Sa Thị. The whole place smells of pitch and wet hemp.
Art brief: A small painted miniature on low forest ground near a river. At its front, the signature gate: two upturned boat hulls standing on end, dark-tarred, keels meeting in a pointed arch. Behind it a short climb of dark timber halls under grey-tile roofs, stacked oars and coiled rope, topped by a three-roof watch pagoda, the tallest outline. A pale shell path runs toward the footprint edge, where a sliver of riverbank and one slipway show. Warm golden-hour light from the top left glinting on the tar. No text, no people larger than specks, nothing outside the footprint.

Rules:
- Paint the place as a small, finely detailed miniature, as if a model-maker had built it into this painted relief: seen from above at a gentle angle so roofs, walls and towers read clearly, its base sitting naturally on the terrain that is there (follow the slopes, the shore, the river).
- Keep it centred and compact: the whole place fits inside a circle about 20 % of the image width across the centre. Short roads or paths may lead out of it.
- Match the map exactly: the same golden-hour light from the TOP LEFT with soft shadows to the bottom right, the same painterly style, colours and level of detail as the surrounding terrain; the building scale fits the trees and hills around it.
- Leave everything outside that central circle exactly as it is in the input.
- Never: text, labels, banners with writing, flags with symbols, people larger than specks, a frame, a vignette, clouds over the place.
